draft.title: Technology and jobs
card: New technology can do some tasks faster or more cheaply than people. Some jobs shrink or disappear as a result, such as checkout work when self-serve machines are used.
Technology also creates new jobs. People are needed to design, build, run and fix it, in areas such as software and data.
The jobs lost and the jobs created often need different skills. A checkout worker may not have the skills for a software job straight away.
Because technology keeps changing, workers may need to learn new skills over time. They can do this through training or study.
draft.remember: Technology removes some jobs and creates others, so workers keep learning new skills.

a.q: A supermarket in Perth installs self-serve checkouts and needs fewer checkout staff. What does this show about technology and jobs?
opts: Technology can remove some jobs
Technology creates jobs in every business
Technology makes workers' skills last longer
Technology only changes the pay of workers
a.why: Self-serve machines do work that checkout staff once did, so some jobs shrink. Technology does create new jobs, but this example shows a job being removed, not one created in this business.
a.clue: Look at what happened to the checkout staff.

b.q: A Hobart bank uses an app that handles many customer requests. It hires more data analysts to run the app and needs fewer tellers. What should a teller who wants to move into the new work do?
opts: Learn new skills, such as working with data
Wait, because the old skills will fit the new jobs
Move to a business that has not used technology
Expect the bank to stop using the app
b.why: The new jobs need different skills from teller work, so the teller needs to learn new ones through training or study. Waiting is tempting, but the card says the lost jobs and new jobs often need different skills.
b.clue: The new jobs and the old jobs need different skills.

b.best: Learn new skills, such as working with data

problems.detail: The remember line says workers 'keep learning new skills', stated as certain. The card says workers 'may need to learn new skills over time'. Hedge it, for example 'so workers may need to learn new skills'.

The right option is the only hedged one ('can remove some jobs'). The distractors are all absolute ('only changes the pay', 'creates jobs in every business', 'makes skills last longer'), so a student can pick the answer from the wording alone.

The right option is the only one with a precise detail ('such as working with data'), which echoes 'data analysts' in the stem. The distractors are clearly weak, so the answer can be picked without knowing the idea.
